cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm coordinating the pickups. Your mum is at the station; her birthday parcel is at the depot that shuts at six. Which comes first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum first, exactly. Then you can tell her the present stays locked up tonight. Would you prefer the parcel first instead?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the parcel. I'll keep Mum company on the phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good teamwork; that's the route. She's ringing me now, though. You decide: I stop to explain we're following your plan, or keep driving and leave her call unanswered?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 coordinates confidently; A3 endorses B choice then offers reversal, and A5 adopts B new plan while returning its communication conflict for B decision.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 mother priority causes A3 parcel consequence; B4 parcel/call solution causes A5 incoming-call-versus-deadline choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 knows Mum preference and B4 offers company by phone, both useful practical contributions.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns the chosen collection plan into a second urgent decision involving the same waiting person.

specificity.evidence: A1 station, depot and six oclock establish the competing responsibilities.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 following your plan has a defensive edge, but the practical call choice remains clear.
